title: Marie Curie: The Greatest Scientist of All Time?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: To find something for the first time.
The natural process by which some substances give off energy.
Careful study or investigation to learn new information.
A basic substance that cannot be broken down into simpler substances.
A prestigious international award given for achievements in science, literature, or peace.
A scientific test done to learn or prove something.
The power that comes from physical or chemical processes and can cause change.

sentences.en: Today, we’re diving into the fascinating life of Marie Skłodowska Curie.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将深入探讨 Marie Skłodowska Curie 迷人的一生。

sentences.en: Was she the greatest scientist ever? Well… maybe!
sentences.zh: 她是有史以来最伟大的科学家吗？嗯……也许吧！

sentences.en: She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields, and a true pioneer in the study of radioactivity.
sentences.zh: 她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性，也是唯一一位在两个不同科学领域获得诺贝尔奖的人，并且是放射性研究真正的先驱。

sentences.en: In this episode, we’ll explore her life, achievements, struggles, and lasting legacy of one of the most influential scientists of all time.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将探讨这位有史以来最具影响力的科学家之一的一生、成就、奋斗历程以及她留下的不朽遗产。

sentences.en: Marie Skłodowska- Curie was born Maria Skłodowska in 1867 in Warsaw, Poland.
sentences.zh: Marie Skłodowska-Curie 于 1867 年出生于波兰华沙，原名 Maria Skłodowska。

sentences.en: She grew up in a family of teachers who valued education deeply.
sentences.zh: 她在极其重视教育的教师家庭中长大。

sentences.en: Her father taught maths and physics and made sure to educate his children in the sciences.
sentences.zh: 她的父亲是一名数学和物理老师，并确保让孩子们接受科学教育。

sentences.en: However, the Skłodowska family faced financial struggles, which made life challenging.
sentences.zh: 然而，Skłodowska 一家面临着经济困难，这让生活充满了挑战。

sentences.en: While Maria showed a strong curiosity and love for learning from a young age, as a woman in the late 19th century, she faced significant barriers.
sentences.zh: 尽管玛丽从小就表现出强烈的好奇心和对学习的热爱，但作为 19 世纪末的女性，她面临着巨大的阻碍。

sentences.en: Women were largely excluded from formal higher education in Poland, and most of the world, at that time.
sentences.zh: 在当时的波兰以及世界大部分地区，女性基本上被排除在正规高等教育之外。

sentences.en: While working as a teacher and tutor, she actually joined a secret, underground school in Warsaw called the Flying University.
sentences.zh: 在当教师和家教的同时，她实际上加入了华沙一所名为“飞行大学”的秘密地下学校。

sentences.en: The Flying University was set up to educate young Polish people, including women, in a Polish style education.
sentences.zh: “飞行大学”的成立是为了向包括女性在内的波兰年轻一代提供波兰风格的教育。

sentences.en: At the time, Poland was part of the Russian Empire, which wanted to control the education system.
sentences.zh: 当时，波兰是俄罗斯帝国的一部分，俄国人企图控制教育系统。

sentences.en: Maria’s experience at the Flying University allowed her to pursue advanced learning despite the restrictions of her society.
sentences.zh: 尽管受到社会限制，玛丽在“飞行大学”的经历还是让她得以继续深造。

sentences.en: In 1891, Maria moved to Paris to study at the Sorbonne, the University of Paris.
sentences.zh: 1891 年，玛丽搬到巴黎，在巴黎大学（即索邦大学）求学。

sentences.en: She had little money, had to learn French (and became known by the French version of her name, Marie) and struggled with the cold Parisian winters.
sentences.zh: 她身无分文，不得不学习法语（后来被称为她名字的法文版 Marie），还要熬过巴黎寒冷的冬天。

sentences.en: In fact, she famously had to wear all her clothes at the same time just to stay warm in the winter.
sentences.zh: 事实上，据传她为了在冬天保暖，不得不把所有的衣服同时穿在身上。

sentences.en: But she remained determined to keep studying, and eventually became one of the top students in her class being awarded multiple degrees.
sentences.zh: 但她依然决心坚持学习，最终以名列前茅的成绩毕业，并获得了多个学位。

sentences.en: In Paris Marie met Pierre Curie, a physicist who shared her deep interest in experimental science.
sentences.zh: 在巴黎，玛丽遇到了 Pierre Curie，一位与她同样对实验科学有着浓厚兴趣的物理学家。

sentences.en: They married in 1895, and their partnership became one of the most famous scientific collaborations in history.
sentences.zh: 他们于 1895 年结婚，这段伴侣关系成为了历史上最著名的科学合作之一。

sentences.en: Together they explored the phenomenon of radioactivity, which wasn’t called radioactivity at that time, but had been recently discovered by Henri Becquerel.
sentences.zh: 他们共同探索了放射性现象——当时不叫放射性，而是最近由亨利·贝克勒尔发现的。

sentences.en: Marie’s approach to research involved measuring tiny amounts of radiation emitted by different substances.
sentences.zh: 玛丽的研究方法涉及测量不同物质发射的微量辐射。

sentences.en: She developed highly precise instruments to detect and measure radiation levels.
sentences.zh: 她开发了高度精确的仪器来检测和测量辐射水平。

sentences.en: Through countless experiments, often with limited funding and basic equipment, the Curies made extraordinary discoveries.
sentences.zh: 通过无数次的实验，通常是在资金有限和设备简陋的情况下，居里夫妇做出了非凡的发现。

sentences.en: In 1898, they isolated two new elements.
sentences.zh: 1898 年，他们分离出了两种新元素。

sentences.en: The first was polonium named after Marie’s homeland of Poland.
sentences.zh: 第一种是钋（polonium），以玛丽的祖国波兰命名。

sentences.en: Later that same year, they discovered radium a substance far more radioactive than uranium.
sentences.zh: 同年晚些时候，他们发现了镭（radium），这是一种放射性远超铀的物质。

sentences.en: To isolate radium Marie painstakingly processed massive amounts of a mineral known as pitchblende.
sentences.zh: 为了分离出镭，玛丽辛苦地处理了大量被称为沥青铀矿的矿石。

sentences.en: Pitchblende was radioactive, and Marie noticed that it was actually more radioactive than uranium.
sentences.zh: 沥青铀矿具有放射性，玛丽注意到它的放射性实际上比铀还要强。

sentences.en: From this mineral, Marie was able to extract tiny amounts of radium.
sentences.zh: 从这种矿石中，玛丽得以提取出微量的镭。

sentences.en: Her work required a lot of patience, precision, and also courage.
sentences.zh: 她的工作需要极大的耐心、精确度，还有勇气。

sentences.en: She was constantly exposed to radiation without knowing its long-term effects.
sentences.zh: 在不知道长期影响的情况下，她长期暴露在辐射中。

sentences.en: Through this research, Marie also coined the term radioactivity.
sentences.zh: 通过这项研究，玛丽还创造了“放射性”一词。

sentences.en: Radioactivity is the property by which certain substances spontaneously emit energy.
sentences.zh: 放射性是指某些物质自发释放能量的属性。

sentences.en: This concept opened the door to entirely new fields of physics and chemistry.
sentences.zh: 这一概念为物理学和化学开辟了全新的领域。

sentences.en: The Curies work demonstrated that atoms were not indivisible.
sentences.zh: 居里夫妇的工作证明了原子并非不可分割。

sentences.en: In other words, atoms could break down and could release energy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，原子可以分解并释放能量。

sentences.en: In recognition of these achievements, Marie and Pierre, along with Henri Becquerel, were awarded the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics.
sentences.zh: 为了表彰这些成就，玛丽、皮埃尔和亨利·贝克勒尔共同荣获 1903 年诺贝尔物理学奖。

sentences.en: Marie Skłodowska Curie became the first woman ever to win a Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: Marie Skłodowska Curie 成为历史上第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。

sentences.en: Their discoveries transformed the understanding of energy and laid the foundation for nuclear physics, radiology, and cancer treatments.
sentences.zh: 他们的发现改变了对能量的理解，并为核物理学、放射学和癌症治疗奠定了基础。

sentences.en: Tragically, Pierre Curie passed away in 1906.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，Pierre Curie 于 1906 年去世。

sentences.en: Marie decided to continue their research alone.
sentences.zh: 玛丽决定独自继续他们的研究。

sentences.en: She took up her husband’s old position as Professor, becoming the first woman to teach at the Sorbonne in Paris.
sentences.zh: 她接替了丈夫生前的教授职位，成为巴黎索邦大学第一位女教师。

sentences.en: In her research, she focused on understanding the nature of radioactivity and investigating the properties of the elements she had discovered.
sentences.zh: 在研究中，她专注于理解放射性的本质，并研究她所发现的元素属性。

sentences.en: Radium and polonium. She was able to measure radioactive decay, study half lives, and observe how radiation affected other things, other substances.
sentences.zh: 镭和钋。她能够测量放射性衰变、研究半衰期，并观察辐射如何影响其他事物、其他物质。

sentences.en: For example, she discovered that radium could constantly produce heat even without an external energy source.
sentences.zh: 例如，她发现镭甚至在没有外部能源的情况下也能持续产生热量。

sentences.en: This showed that atoms could release energy spontaneously, a concept that led to the entire field of nuclear physics.
sentences.zh: 这表明原子可以自发释放能量，这个概念催生了整个核物理学领域。

sentences.en: She also studied the power of different types of radiation to penetrate different objects.
sentences.zh: 她还研究了不同类型的辐射穿透不同物体的能力。

sentences.en: This later led to the development of medical imaging, for example x-ray machines, which use radiation to look at your bones inside your body.
sentences.zh: 这随后催生了医学影像学的发展，例如利用辐射来观察体内骨骼的 X 光机。

sentences.en: And radiology, including cancer treatments, radiotherapy, ways to kill cancer inside your body.
sentences.zh: 还有放射学，包括癌症治疗、放射疗法以及消灭体内癌细胞的方法。

sentences.en: In 1911, Marie Skłodowska- Curie received her second Nobel Prize this time in Chemistry.
sentences.zh: 1911 年，Marie Skłodowska-Curie 获得了她的第二个诺贝尔奖，这一次是化学奖。

sentences.en: The prize recognized her discoveries and studies of radium and polonium.
sentences.zh: 该奖项肯定了她对镭和钋的发现与研究。

sentences.en: She was the first person to win two prizes in two different fields.
sentences.zh: 她是第一位在两个不同领域两次获奖的人。

sentences.en: During World War I, Marie used her knowledge of radiation to save lives on the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战期间，玛丽利用她对放射性的知识在战场上拯救生命。

sentences.en: She recognized that x-ray technology, which had advanced thanks to her studies of radioactivity, could be used to diagnose injuries or locate bullets and shrapnel inside soldiers’ bodies.
sentences.zh: 她认识到，由于她对放射性的研究而取得进展的 X 射线技术可用于诊断受伤情况或定位士兵体内的子弹和弹片。

sentences.en: X-Ray technology allows you to see inside a body, which is obviously an incredibly useful thing in the middle of a war.
sentences.zh: X 射线技术能让你看清体内部，这在战争期间显然是一项极其有用的技术。

sentences.en: Marie developed mobile X-ray units, which became known as “Little Curies “.
sentences.zh: 玛丽开发了移动式 X 射线车，被称为“小居里”（Little Curies）。

sentences.en: These were small, portable X-ray machines that could be transported to hospitals and even directly to the battlefield.
sentences.zh: 这些是小型便携式 X 光机，可以运送到医院，甚至直接送到战场前线。

sentences.en: She trained teams of women, including nurses and students to operate the machines, ensuring that wounded soldiers could be treated quickly and accurately.
sentences.zh: 她培训了一支由女性（包括护士和学生）组成的团队来操作这些机器，确保受伤士兵能够得到迅速、准确的治疗。

sentences.en: By the end of the war, it is estimated that Curie’s mobile units had treated hundreds of thousands of injured soldiers.
sentences.zh: 到战争结束时，据估计居里夫人的移动医疗车已经治疗了数十万名受伤士兵。

sentences.en: In her later years, Marie Skłodowska- Curie continued her research as well as visiting numerous countries to give speeches.
sentences.zh: 晚年时，Marie Skłodowska-Curie 继续她的研究，并访问了许多国家进行演讲。

sentences.en: For example, she met the US President Warren G Harding in 1921.
sentences.zh: 例如，她于 1921 年会见了美国总统沃伦·G·哈定。

sentences.en: She also established institutions to continue her work.
sentences.zh: 她还建立了一些机构来延续她的工作。

sentences.en: In 1914, she helped found the Radium Institute in Paris, which became a leading center for research in physics and chemistry and medicine.
sentences.zh: 1914 年，她协助在巴黎创立了镭研究所，该研究所后来成为物理学、化学和医学研究的顶尖中心。

sentences.en: She also worked with the League of Nations, a kind of early attempt at creating an organization similar to the UN.
sentences.zh: 她还与国际联盟合作，这是创建类似联合国组织的一种早期尝试。

sentences.en: She founded the Curie Foundation in Paris, and also the Radium Institute in Warsaw, her hometown.
sentences.zh: 她在巴黎创立了居里基金会，并在她的家乡华沙创立了镭研究所。

sentences.en: Marie Skłodowska Curie’s influence extended far beyond her research.
sentences.zh: Marie Skłodowska Curie 的影响远远超出了她的研究范畴。

sentences.en: She was a trailblazer for women in science.
sentences.zh: 她是科学界女性的先驱。

sentences.en: She was the first female professor at the Sorbonne and the first woman to win Nobel Prizes.
sentences.zh: 她是索邦大学第一位女教授，也是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。

sentences.en: In fact, her daughter Irene went on also to become a highly respected scientist and actually the discoverer of artificial radioactivity.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她的女儿 Irene 后来也成为了一位备受尊敬的科学家，并且实际上是人工放射性的发现者。

sentences.en: So the Curie family were a group of incredibly respected and successful experimental scientists.
sentences.zh: 所以居里家族是一群备受尊敬且极为成功的实验科学家。

sentences.en: Marie Skłodowska- Curie passed away in 1934 from aplastic anemia.
sentences.zh: Marie Skłodowska-Curie 于 1934 年死于再生障碍性贫血。

sentences.en: Aplastic anemia was almost certainly caused by her years of researching radiation.
sentences.zh: 再生障碍性贫血几乎可以肯定是她多年研究辐射造成的。

sentences.en: At the beginning, the Curies, the scientific community had no idea how dangerous radiation and radioactivity and exposure to elements like radium could be to your health.
sentences.zh: 最初，居里夫妇和科学界根本不知道辐射、放射性以及接触镭等元素会对健康造成多大的危害。

sentences.en: Today, Curie is remembered for her extraordinary discoveries, for coining the term radioactivity and also for her humanitarian work in creating x-ray machines and helping during World War I.
sentences.zh: 今天，人们铭记居里夫人是因为她非凡的发现、她创造了“放射性”一词，以及她在第一次世界大战期间制造 X 光机和参与救援的人道主义工作。

sentences.en: Was Marie Skłodowska Curie the greatest scientist ever?
sentences.zh: Marie Skłodowska Curie 是有史以来最伟大的科学家吗？

sentences.en: Her scientific achievements were groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 她的科学成就是开创性的。

sentences.en: She discovered two new elements. She coined the term radioactivity.
sentences.zh: 她发现了两种新元素。她创造了“放射性”一词。

sentences.en: And she conducted experiments that laid the foundation for nuclear physics, chemistry, and medical treatments.
sentences.zh: 她进行的实验为核物理学、化学和医学治疗奠定了基础。

sentences.en: She did all of this at a time when women were largely excluded from science.
sentences.zh: 她所有这一切都是在女性被大面积排除在科学界之外的时期完成的。

sentences.en: And she also actively wanted to keep using her Polish name, her maiden name we would say in English, which is why in this episode I have tried to say Marie Skłodowska-Curie, instead of just saying Marie Curie, because Marie Skłodowska-Curie wanted her name to be remembered as Skłodowska-Curie.
sentences.zh: 而且她还积极想要使用她的波兰名字，我们在英语中称之为娘家姓，这就是为什么在本期节目中我一直试图说 Marie Skłodowska-Curie，而不是只说 Marie Curie，因为 Marie Skłodowska-Curie 希望人们记住她的名字是 Skłodowska-Curie。

sentences.en: When we compare Marie with other great scientists like Isaac Newton, Albert Einstein, or Charles Darwin, I think it’s really difficult to decide if one person is greater than the other.
sentences.zh: 当我们把玛丽与其他伟大科学家（如艾萨克·牛顿、阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦或查尔斯·达尔文）进行比较时，我认为很难决定某一个人是否比另一个人更伟大。

sentences.en: For example, I did an episode on Isaac Newton a few months ago.
sentences.zh: 例如，几个月前我做了一期关于艾萨克·牛顿的节目。

sentences.en: You can go listen to it. It’s one of the first video episodes of Thinking in English.
sentences.zh: 你可以去听听。那是《Thinking in English》最早的视频节目之一。

sentences.en: And Isaac Newton in one year changed the way that we understand physics and forces and gravity.
sentences.zh: 艾萨克·牛顿在短短一年内就改变了我们对物理学、力和引力的理解。

sentences.en: He completely revolutionized science. Albert Einstein did similar things, completely changing the way that Newton’s physics worked.
sentences.zh: 他彻底彻底革新了科学。阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦也做了类似的事情，彻底改变了牛顿物理学的运作方式。

sentences.en: And Marie Curie… her discoveries laid the foundations for so many other things.
sentences.zh: 而玛丽·居里……她的发现为如此之多的其他领域奠定了基础。

sentences.en: While it’s difficult to definitely crown anyone as the greatest, Marie Skłodowska Curie’s combination of groundbreaking discoveries and her social or societal impact definitely makes her one of the most remarkable scientists in history.
sentences.zh: 虽然很难明确加冕任何人是最伟大的，但 Marie Skłodowska Curie 兼具开创性的发现和她对社会的深远影响，绝对使她成为历史上最卓越的科学家之一。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Who do you consider to be the greatest scientist of all time?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你认为谁是有史以来最伟大的科学家？
